name: Tough74 V2 Wear-resistant Tough Resin
verdict:
BRIDGES: ALL FOUR HOLD (V: “all OK”). Measured from the model, the gaps between the supports are 2 / 4 / 6 and 8 mm, so the longest span with no sag is 8 mm.

⚠️ 8 mm is the MODEL's ceiling, not the resin's limit. There is no longer gap in this model, so the real limit lies somewhere above it and stays unmeasured. Against other resins this reads as “held everything it was given”, not “can do no more”.

⭐ Why it matters in practice: the bridge is the only one of the three simple models that measures an OVERHANG - whether a layer carries itself with nothing underneath. That is what decides how many supports real prints will need. 8 mm with no sag is a quarter of the length of our plate (40.8 x 30.6 mm).
future: Resione pointed out that this printer has no pre-exposure wait - a pause before the UV comes on that lets a viscous resin flow back under the part. The firmware does not have it yet, and it is going into a future release. All the test prints so far came out true without it.
about: Resione's tough, wear-resistant resin: stiff and hard rather than brittle, and smooth straight off the plate.
take: Sharp down to the pixel limit, and a printed clip took 25 cycles without cracking. A 21 mm lattice cube printed standing on its corner came out square, every face at 21 mm.
stageNote: The lattice cube used at first came from another test set and turned out to be deformed, so a true cube was built from scratch. The first prints still leaned. A series of matched cubes printed since then came out square, and a 21 mm cube standing on its corner measured 21 mm on every face.

tests.txt: Eight bars from 4.0 to 16.0 s. Dry and crisp from 7.0 s; 8.5 s taken forward.
Six of seven pillars straight and the detail clean, but it gripped the plate too hard to lift.

props.v: too strong - cannot be lifted without freezing

tests.txt: One step up at 10.0 s: the thinnest pillar stands in three rows, slots open, and base 40 s releases cleanly. The profile is built on these.

props.q: Thinnest pillar straight up to row

props.v: good - held for the whole print

tests.txt: Hardest first layer we have - 61 % of the plate in one layer. It held, and came off normally.
A spring clip pushed on and off 25 times. No cracks, still springs back.

props.q: Pushes on and off without cracking

tests.txt: Pins down to 0.30 mm all stood - 2.3 pixels wide. Below that the screen runs out, not the resin.
Unsupported spans of 2, 4, 6 and 8 mm. All four held with no sag.
Lattice cube standing on its corner, 20 mm. The grid stayed open all the way through.
The same lattice at 28 mm. 0.51 mm walls came out clean, but the cube itself leans.
